# Lecture slides for two cohorts, week by week {.unnumbered}

::: mk-hero-sub
Everything used to teach the quantitative part of **MK-068-EN Empirical
Research Methods** at Justus Liebig University Giessen: a prerequisites sheet
and seven weeks of lectures, taught in Winter Semester 2023/24 and again,
revised, in Winter Semester 2024/25. The 2024/25 decks are published as
interactive slides rendered from their source; the slides of both cohorts are
available as the PDFs that were shared with students on Ilias.
:::

::: mk-hero-meta
[Taught and written by Eduard Bukin](https://www.uni-giessen.de/faculties/f09/institutes/agri/policy/team/bukin) ·
[Institute of Agricultural Policy and Market Research](https://www.uni-giessen.de/faculties/f09/institutes/agri/policy) ·
[Source on GitHub](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/)
:::
:::

## Two cohorts

the two runs, so the cohorts are kept apart: pick the one you attended.

## Week by week

Each week page brings together the interactive deck, the PDFs of both cohorts,
the slide sources and the data behind them.

```{=html}
<div class="mk-grid">

  <div class="mk-card is-reading">
    <span class="mk-card-kicker">Week 0</span>
    <h3 class="mk-card-title"><a href="weeks/week-00.html">Prerequisites</a></h3>
    <p class="mk-card-desc">What to refresh before weeks 1 to 3, with pre-recorded lectures and Khan Academy units, and the additional reading list.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mk-card is-slide">
    <span class="mk-card-kicker">Week 1</span>
    <h3 class="mk-card-title"><a href="weeks/week-01.html">Introduction. Descriptive statistics</a></h3>
    <p class="mk-card-desc">Population and sample, sampling designs, description versus inference; then central tendency, outliers, weighted means and box plots.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mk-card is-slide">
    <span class="mk-card-kicker">Week 2</span>
    <h3 class="mk-card-title"><a href="weeks/week-02.html">Distribution, variance and its applications</a></h3>
    <p class="mk-card-desc">Density and cumulative distributions, the Lorenz curve, variance and standard deviation, quantiles, z-scores and the WHO stunting standards.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mk-card is-slide">
    <span class="mk-card-kicker">Week 3</span>
    <h3 class="mk-card-title"><a href="weeks/week-03.html">Bi-variate data. Correlation and causation</a></h3>
    <p class="mk-card-desc">Scatter plots, trend lines, the correlation coefficient and its pitfalls, and the step from correlation to cause, effect and ceteris paribus.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mk-card is-slide">
    <span class="mk-card-kicker">Week 4</span>
    <h3 class="mk-card-title"><a href="weeks/week-04.html">Cause and effect in the RCT. Hypothesis testing. t-tests</a></h3>
    <p class="mk-card-desc">Null and alternative hypotheses, the two error types, p-values, and t-tests applied to deworming and conditional cash transfer experiments.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mk-card is-slide">
    <span class="mk-card-kicker">Week 5</span>
    <h3 class="mk-card-title"><a href="weeks/week-05.html">Central Limit Theorem. t-distribution. Confidence intervals</a></h3>
    <p class="mk-card-desc">From the population distribution to the sampling distribution of the mean, standard errors, confidence intervals and one- and two-sample t-tests.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mk-card is-slide">
    <span class="mk-card-kicker">Week 6</span>
    <h3 class="mk-card-title"><a href="weeks/week-06.html">Simple and multiple regression. Bias. Linearity</a></h3>
    <p class="mk-card-desc">The regression line and OLS, coefficient interpretation and inference, multiple regression, bias versus efficiency, the six assumptions and linearity.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="mk-card is-slide">
    <span class="mk-card-kicker">Week 7</span>
    <h3 class="mk-card-title"><a href="weeks/week-07.html">Multiple linear regression. Practice</a></h3>
    <p class="mk-card-desc">Three worked examples end to end: hedonic land prices, a rice production function, and returns to fertiliser in a field experiment.</p>
  </div>

</div>
```

## How the materials are labelled

The same icons are used in the sidebar and on every page:

| Icon | Material |
|:--:|:--|
| 🖥 | Interactive slides: a revealjs deck rendered from the `.qmd` source, opens full screen |
| 📄 | PDF slides, exactly as shared with the cohort on Ilias |
| 💻 | Slide source on GitHub (`.qmd`), at the commit that matches the cohort |
| 📊 | A dataset used in the slides, with its provenance |
| 📖 | A reading or a reference |
| 📺 | A video |

## About this site

This site collects the lecture materials for the quantitative part of
**MK-068-EN (TM) Empirical Research Methods** at the Institute of Agricultural
Policy and Market Research, JLU Giessen. It does not replace the Ilias course
page, where the course was run; it makes the slides readable, searchable and
downloadable on any device, and keeps the two cohorts' versions side by side.

Written and taught by
**[Eduard Bukin](https://www.uni-giessen.de/faculties/f09/institutes/agri/policy/team/bukin)**.
All materials are open source and available
[on GitHub](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/).
